Comprehensive sexuality education · 2026 mapping

Where UNFPA delivers CSE — and what each country calls it

Six regional office returns and the Arab States evaluation survey, reconciled into one record per business unit. Scroll: the map answers one question at a time.

Scroll ↓

The population 0

business units are in the mapping

Six regional offices, every country office under them, and two rows that are offices rather than countries. The sheet returned 138 rows: one country office filed twice, and it is counted once here. This is the denominator for everything that follows.

Who answered 0

have not returned it

102 answered. The 35 in grey are not units without CSE — they are units without an answer. Five of them are the Gulf states, and they are missing as a block, not at random.

Who delivers 0

deliver comprehensive sexuality education

Of the 102 that answered, 86 say yes and 15 say no. One answered everything except that question, so it sits in neither column.

The finding 0

call it CSE, and nothing else

The map has switched to local terminology. Twenty-four more use the term alongside another one.

Forty-six use a different name entirely — life skills education, family life education, healthy lifestyle, reproductive health education.

Where the name disappears 0

of the fifteen Arab States offices use the term CSE

Their most common terms are SRH education and life skills education, eight offices each, then reproductive health education with seven.

A portfolio filtered on the word “CSE” would lose most of this region.

Global programmes 0

countries sit in a globally supported programme

EmpowerED reaches ten, the Global Programme on out-of-school CSE reaches twelve, and seven countries are in both. The six regional offices also carry EmpowerED.

Everything else on this map is country-led, and that is the point of the exercise.
